observations: body L1, L5, L12: specks between «linearis» and «pla-» (L1), at the left of the display of L5 and over the u of «tangentibus» (L12) are not transcribed.

body L1-L10: the displays agree with one another: diametrus planetae : diametrus Terrae = 5 1/2 × r/R × δ/Δ = r × δ/Δ : (R : 5 1/2), and 1108 : 5 1/2 = 2216 : 11 = 201 5/11, as printed. «Albatenii» (L8) is letter-spaced.

body L12-L21: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the epicycle about O; the tangents XA and XB from the eye X, each running on beyond its point of contact; the line XO, ending a little above O; the dotted radius OB dash by dash, its first dash joined to the top of XO and its last to the tangent at B, as printed; the bold italic letters O, A, B, X. On the print XA touches the circle (O stands 29.73 pt from it, the radius being 29.72 pt), XB stands 0.3 pt outside it, and XO passes 0.3 pt to the right of O.

body L13-L16, L20: «Ptolemaeus» (L16, L20) is letter-spaced; the dashes before «In Mercurio» (L13), «Aliter» (L15) and «In Iove» (L20) measure 10.1, 10.3 and 10.0 pt, and «al–Battānī» (L15) has a long dash (5.3 pt).

body L17-L24: 39ᵖ 30′ : 60ᵖ = 0,658333 = sin 41° 10′ 22″, so that OXB = 41° 10′ ½ to the half minute and AXB = 82° 20′ 45″, 82° 21′. 11ᵖ 30′ : 60ᵖ = 0,191666 = sin 11° 3′ 0″: the printed «0,19666» stands for 0,19166, from which OXB = 11° 3′ and AXB = 22° 6′ (L22) follow; 0,19666 would give 11° 20′ ½. 6ᵖ 30′ : 60ᵖ = 0,108333 = sin 6° 13′ 9″, and AXB = 12° 26′ 18″, 12° 26′. The printed numbers are kept. The dots after «0,65833» are four, after «0,19666» five and after «0.10833» four; «0.10833» has a full stop for the decimal comma of L18 and L21.

body L22-L24: «Ptolemaeus» (L23) is letter-spaced; the dash before «In Saturno» (L22) measures 10.4 pt, and the dash before «Schiaparelli» (L24), 9.8 pt, follows the full stop without a space. A heavy bracket closes Schiaparelli's addition, opened on p. 289, L35; the feet of the two L of «Schiaparelli» print apart from their stems, like «SCHIAPAREL.I.I», and its full stop prints small.
body L25-L27: «Tycho Brahe» is letter-spaced; «467–71», «al–Farghānī» and «al–Battānī» (L27) have long dashes (5.2, 5.5 and 5.3 pt).
body L30, L37: the dashes after «c)» and «d)» measure 10.2 and 10.0 pt; «18–20» and «20–30» have long dashes (5.3 and 5.4 pt).

body L31-L36: heavy brackets open (L31) and close (L36) Schiaparelli's note; «al–Battānī» (L34) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.4 pt), and the dash before «Schiaparelli» (L36) measures 10.2 pt. Al-Battānī's greatest equation of the centre of the Sun is 1° 59′ 10″ (p. 213), twice which is 3° 58′; his diameters of the Sun, 31′ 20″ at the apogee and 33′ 40″ at the perigee (translation, p. 58), have the mean 32′ 30″. The translation gives 39° 48′ at p. 122, l. 33, with Plato's 49° 48′ (note 19), and at p. 123, l. 21, with Plato's 9° 48′ (note 4).
body L38-L40: a heavy bracket opens the addition (L38); «al–Battānī» (L39) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.3 pt).
